raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Same fix as #59848, for DSv4.1. Default `cpu_offload` Engram tables use `pin_memory=True`, which rounds each table up to a power of two. Register them at exact size through the existing THP helper, without huge pages. cc @Juntian777: if you can run your #59327 lookup bench on GB200, it would show whether the GB10 speedup carries over; it doesn't block this PR.

## Claims

- TP2 per-rank table: 66 → 47.2 GiB host memory.
- GB10 lookup kernel: ~1.8× faster unsorted, 7–21% faster with #59327's sort.
- RTX PRO 6000 (PCIe): same memory saving, lookup speed unchanged.

## Validation

GB10, Engram lookup kernel, TP4 per-rank table, 32K tokens:

| memory | host | unsorted | sorted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pin_memory` (before) | 33.1 GiB | 41.4 ms | 10.9 ms |
| exact `cudaHostAlloc` | 24.9 GiB | 41.4 ms | 10.9 ms |
| registered (this PR) | 24.3 GiB | 22.7 ms | 10.2 ms |

Exact size gives the memory saving; on GB10 the registered memory type gives the speed. These are 4 KiB pages, not THP.

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (PCIe Gen5 x16), same bench, TP4 per-rank table, 32K tokens:

| memory | host | unsorted | sorted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pin_memory` (before) | 33.1 GiB | 14.9 ms | 11.2 ms |
| exact `cudaHostAlloc` | 24.7 GiB | 14.9 ms | 11.2 ms |
| registered (this PR) | 24.7 GiB | 14.9 ms | 11.2 ms |

Over PCIe the memory type makes no difference to speed, so the speedup is specific to GB10's coherent C2C link. GB200 has the same kind of link but isn't measured.

`pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py`: 116 passed on GB10. After rebasing onto #63009, 129 passed and 3 skipped (multi-GPU) on one RTX PRO 6000; the same files on main fail only the new small-page case.

Still needed before un-drafting: an E2E `cpu_offload` run.

## Details

- `_allocate_huge_page_storage(n)` → `_allocate_registered_storage(n, huge_pages)`, called once. The THP path and the sort are unchanged. A failed registration falls back to `pin_memory=True`.
- CUDA only; ROCm is unchanged. #63009 already allocates ROCm tables at their exact size, via huge pages.
- Why not just `use_thp`: it already registers at exact size, but it is opt-in and skips the sort, so default users were left with the rounding.
- Why not `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=pinned_max_round_threshold_mb`: it gets the same exact size, but only for users who know to set it, and on GB10 it misses the faster lookup (the `cudaHostAlloc` rows above). Over PCIe it is equivalent.

<details><summary>All runs</summary>

```
TP4 (6 heads x 16Mi rows):
pinned     unsorted: 4096:5193us 8192:10355us 16384:20704us 32768:41424us
pinned     sorted:   4096:5190us 8192:4198us 16384:6680us 32768:10892us
exact-cudaHostAlloc unsorted: 4096:5196us 8192:10367us 16384:20732us 32768:41443us
exact-cudaHostAlloc sorted:   4096:5191us 8192:4220us 16384:6707us 32768:10919us
registered unsorted: 4096:2855us 8192:5695us 16384:11371us 32768:22715us
registered sorted:   4096:2850us 8192:3729us 16384:6173us 32768:10234us
TP2 (12 heads x 16Mi rows):
pinned     unsorted: 4096:11851us 8192:23681us 16384:47352us 32768:94698us
registered unsorted: 4096:6294us 8192:12568us 16384:25120us 32768:50220us
pinned     sorted:   4096:5436us 8192:8394us 16384:13443us 32768:21951us
registered sorted:   4096:4492us 8192:7376us 16384:12273us 32768:20410us
```
Median of 48 runs. TP4 4096 is below the sort threshold.

```
RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (PCIe), TP4 (6 heads x 16Mi rows):
pinned     unsorted: 4096:1878us 8192:3739us 16384:7456us 32768:14901us
exact-cudaHostAlloc unsorted: 4096:1880us 8192:3743us 16384:7465us 32768:14914us
registered unsorted: 4096:1878us 8192:3742us 16384:7460us 32768:14907us
pinned     sorted:   4096:1883us 8192:3270us 16384:6080us 32768:11191us
exact-cudaHostAlloc sorted:   4096:1882us 8192:3267us 16384:6085us 32768:11218us
registered sorted:   4096:1880us 8192:3270us 16384:6080us 32768:11205us
```
</details>

-    assert same_storage == registered

+    huge_pages = use_thp or current_platform.is_rocm()

     return error is None
 
 
-def _allocate_huge_page_storage(num_bytes: int) -> torch.Tensor | None:
-    """Register prefaulted huge pages, or return None for pinned-memory fallback."""
+def _allocate_registered_storage(
+    num_bytes: int, huge_pages: bool
+) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+    """Register exact-size host memory, or return None for pinned-memory fallback."""
     if sys.platform != "linux":
         return None
     try:
         mapping = mmap.mmap(-1, num_bytes, flags=mmap.MAP_PRIVATE | mmap.MAP_ANONYMOUS)
-        mapping.madvise(mmap.MADV_HUGEPAGE)
+        if huge_pages:
+            mapping.madvise(mmap.MADV_HUGEPAGE)
     except OSError as exc:
         logger.warning(
-            "Engram huge-page allocation failed (%s); using pinned memory.", exc
+            "Engram host table allocation failed (%s); using pinned memory.", exc
         )
         return None
 
     owner = np.frombuffer(mapping, dtype=np.uint8)
-    # Fault the pages in before CUDA pins them, so they can be huge.
-    owner[:: mmap.PAGESIZE] = 0
+    if huge_pages:
+        # Fault the pages in before CUDA pins them, so they can be huge.
+        owner[:: mmap.PAGESIZE] = 0
     tensor = torch.from_numpy(owner)
     pointer = tensor.data_ptr()
     result = torch.cuda.cudart().cudaHostRegister(pointer, num_bytes, 0)
@@ -1054,13 +1058,16 @@ def _allocate_weights(self) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
                 torch.empty(self.part_num_embeddings, scale_dim, dtype=torch.uint8),
             )
         # pin_memory rounds up to a power of two. ROCm pins huge pages either way.
-        if self.use_thp or current_platform.is_rocm():
+        huge_pages = self.use_thp or current_platform.is_rocm()

             weight_bytes = self.part_num_embeddings * self.dim
-            packed = _allocate_huge_page_storage(

+            packed = _allocate_registered_storage(
+                weight_bytes + weight_bytes // self.block_size, huge_pages=huge_pages
             )
             if packed is not None:
-                self._packed = packed

+                if huge_pages:
+                    self._packed = packed
